extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX/AMS-TeX/plain TeX users who need to typeset graphs and diagrams (mathematicians, computer scientists, diagram authors)
extracted.subtask_short: typesetting diagrams in TeX with Xy-pic
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and feature list for producing and configuring graphs and diagrams in TeX using the Xy-pic package, including available modes, object primitives, backends, and documentation sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic works with most formats, including all variants of LaTeX, AMS-TeX, and plain TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used widely across many application areas; likely already included in common distributions (e.g., TeX Live pictures bundle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel and modular options architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is structured as a kernel and several orthogonal modules called options, each defining a custom notation for a particular kind of graphical object or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modules (options) are combinable and define mnemonic plain text notations for specific graphical classes; choose options appropriate to the diagram type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph combinator mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph combinator mode where diagrams are specified the way they are composed as graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when diagrams are naturally expressed as node-and-edge graphs; focuses on composition semantics rather than explicit coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix-like (diagram) mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix-like mode where the dimensions of the drawing are computed by aligning diagram entries in rows and columns (the diagram mode Xy-pic version 2 users are used to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for commutative diagrams and grid-aligned layouts; entries behave like matrix cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygon mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A polygon mode where diagrams shaped as regular polygons are entered in a simple way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient for symmetric or cyclic diagrams laid out on polygon vertices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knot and link typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: A mode for typesetting beautiful knots and links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized primitives and notation intended for topology/knot diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object-oriented turtle graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: A general object-oriented turtle graphic drawing language for specifying graphs with objects and connections between them in a manner independent of orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for programmatic/directional drawing where relative motion/orientation semantics are convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position specification formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions can be given in a variety of formats (extendable) including user defined coordinates (x,y) and relative to previous positions, objects, object edges, and points on connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexible coordinate/relative positioning supports many layout strategies; extendable formats allow custom coordinate systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object shapes and extensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects may be circular, elliptic, or rectangular (more shapes can be added) and adjusted in several ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default shapes cover common needs; users can add shapes as required for specialized diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large library of mnemonic objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Large library of objects with mnemonic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer library objects for readability; mnemonic names make diagram source easier to maintain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects oriented along connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects that orient themselves along a connection when placed relative to it; e.g., @{|-} is like \vdash but oriented along the connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to place symbols whose orientation should follow the connecting path; new such objects can be defined conveniently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for TeX boxes as objects
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX boxes, i.e., text and mathematical formulae, can be used as objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed complex typeset content directly as node labels or objects in diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc primitives (circle segments and conics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes circle segments and optionally arbitrary elliptical, quadratic, and cubic arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for smooth curved connections and shapes; some features may depend on backend capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection alignment semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections are aligned between the reference points of objects but start and end on the edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures visually correct attachment of connections to object boundaries rather than centers; reference-point based alignment supports predictable placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary objects as connection components
rubrics_metrics.description: Any object can be used to build a connection (using diagonal filling); library objects provide common line types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create custom line styles and connectors by composing objects; reuse library line types where suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible arrow and path notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexible notation for drawing arrows and general paths with tail, stem, and head built from any object(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure arrow tips and parts from arbitrary objects to match symbol styles; supports many stylistic variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced arrow features
rubrics_metrics.description: Special support for arrows that cross each other, arrows that go by other entries, paired arrows (including support for 2-cells), curved arrows, and arrows with bends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these features to express complex relations such as commuting squares, 2-cells, or overlapping edges; pay attention to ordering and layering for crossings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow tip style configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of arrow tips can be configured to match several styles of symbol arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match arrow tip style to the document's mathematical symbols for visual consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library of frames and braces
rubrics_metrics.description: Library of frames and braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frames/braces for grouping or annotating diagram regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations: rotation, scaling, colour, line thickness
rubrics_metrics.description: Special notation for rotation, scaling, colour, and line thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct typesetting of these features requires a backend that supports them; when unsupported Xy-pic tries to approximate so that picture size is stable (and thus page breaks remain consistent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Backend PostScript output
rubrics_metrics.description: Output can use PostScript for drawing (several \special formats are supported: dvips, Textures, and OzTeX - more are being added). Notation for inclusion of literal PostScript is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a PostScript-capable backend to get accurate rendering of advanced graphical features; contact maintainers for the current list of supported drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF output support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for Adobe PDF output is available from version 3.8 (thanks to support by Daniel Müllner and font conversion software by Scott Pakin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use xypdf package and the PDF backend to generate PDF-native drawings; check documentation for required toolchain and font conversion steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for visual integration with TeX typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic has been designed with great care to allow the style of pictures to match well with the exquisite quality of the surrounding TeX typeset material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure fonts, line weights, and symbol styles to harmonize diagrams with surrounding text and math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation behaviour when backend lacks features
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when the backend does not support features like rotation/colour, Xy-pic tries to approximate what is requested so that at least the picture size is stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect visual approximations but reliable layout (important for page breaks); prefer backends that implement the requested features for final output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation suite
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Xy-pic documentation consists of: Xy-pic User's Guide (explains basic matrix-like diagrams), Xy-pic Reference Manual (syntax and drawing semantics), Xy-pic Complete Sources with TeXnical Commentary, and the xypdf package documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the User's Guide for getting started, Reference Manual for detailed syntax, and xypdf docs for PDF specifics; several tutorials and companion texts are available for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorials and external references
rubrics_metrics.description: Several tutorials and papers exist (e.g., An Introduction to Xy-pic; Commutative Diagrams with XY-pic; The LaTeX Graphics Companion chapter on Xy-pic; Using Xy-pic in LyX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look up tutorials for step-by-step examples and domain-specific use cases (category theory, topology, automata, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: You can get Xy-pic from CTAN or directly from the SourceForge development project home; Xy-pic is likely included with many TeX installations (e.g., TeX Live pictures bundle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install via CTAN/TeX Live or fetch latest from SourceForge for development versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: License and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is © by its authors as free software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the project's licensing terms when redistributing or modifying; attribution to authors is noted on the homepage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help and support channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Help and support on Xy-pic matters, as well as announcements of new versions, are provided by the Xy-pic mailing list, graciously hosted by TUG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join the mailing list for usage questions, bug reports, and announcements; community feedback has informed the package for decades.
